source_verification.method: Parsed cached primary XML and read complete structured abstract plus plain language summary; no fresh HTTP and no full article/results-table verification
exact_primary_quotes: All of the included studies investigated food products; none investigated alcohol or tobacco.

For selection outcomes, meta‐analysis of three comparisons from three studies (n = 154) found that exposure to fewer options resulted in a large reduction in selection of the targeted food(s): SMD −1.13 (95% confidence interval (CI) −1.90 to −0.37) (low certainty evidence).

For consumption outcomes, meta‐analysis of 15 comparisons from 12 studies (n = 1098) found that exposure to food placed farther away resulted in a moderate reduction in its consumption: SMD −0.60 (95% CI −0.84 to −0.36) (low certainty evidence).

Meta‐regression analyses indicated that this effect was greater: the farther away the product was placed; when only the targeted product(s) was available; when participants were of low deprivation status; and when the study was at high risk of bias.

intentional_changes: Selection effect remains SMD −1.13 with original CI/n, expressed as selection amount rather than people percentage.
Regression condition is target foods only, not a general simple-choice claim.
All original numerical results retained; no conversion to percentage.
